title: An In vitro System to Gauge the Thrombolytic Efficacy of Histotripsy and a Lytic Drug
protocol: Prepare the clots within 2 weeks but more than 3 days prior to the day of the experiment.
Draw fresh human venous blood.
Aliquot the total blood drawn in 2 mL increments per desired clot.
Transfer each 2 mL aliquot to one Pasteur pipette.
Incubate the blood aliquots within the pipettes in a water bath for 3 h at 37 °C.
Fill the water tank with reverse osmosis water.
Line the bottom surface of the tank with an acoustic absorbing material.
Degas and filter the water using a water handling system.
Place two heating elements at the bottom surface of the tank.
Heat the water to 37.3 °C.
Submerge the flow channel in the water tank to bring it to physiologic temperature during degassing/filtering/heating stage.
Dilute rt-PA obtained from a manufacturer in powdered form to 1 mg/mL in sterile water.
Aliquot 100 µL of diluted rt-PA into 0.5 mL centrifuge tubes and store them at -80 °C.
Aliquot 35 mL of human fresh-frozen type O plasma in 50 mL centrifuge tubes.
Store the tubes at -80 °C.
Retrieve plasma aliquots from the freezer on the experiment day.
Immerse the frozen plasma aliquots in a water bath at 37 °C to thaw (~10 min).
Pour thawed plasma into a beaker that is triply rinsed with ultrapure water.
Lightly cover the mouth of the beaker with aluminum foil to prevent contamination.
Place the beaker in the water bath and allow air contact through loose foil.
Let plasma equilibrate at 37 °C for at least 2 h.
Retrieve frozen rt-PA vials on ice until needed, with one vial for each experiment run.
Dissolve agarose to make a 2% low gelling solution in a 50 mL flask.
Heat the agarose solution in a microwave until it starts bubbling.
Secure the heated flask with a waterproof screw lid.
Submerge the flask in a water bath alongside plasma.
Connect motorized positioners to the runtime environment of a programming platform as per manufacturer directions.
Ensure motors of the system are connected to the appropriate port of the computer running the runtime environment.
Mount the histotripsy source on the motorized positioning system.
Connect the histotripsy source to its driving electronics via specified connectors.
Cover the imaging array with a probe cover.
Affix the array coaxially in the aperture of the histotripsy source.
Connect the imaging array to an ultrasound scanning system.
Submerge the histotripsy source and imaging array into the tank while degassing.
Gently remove any air bubbles using a syringe from the surface of the histotripsy source or imaging array.
Acquire B-mode images at a rate of 20 frames per second using the imaging array.
Adjust the imaging window to ensure visualization of the focus of the histotripsy source in real-time images.
Set the fundamental frequency of the histotripsy source to 1.5 MHz.
Set the pulse repetition frequency to 20-100 Hz.
Set the pulse duration to 1-20 cycles per pulse.
Set the total number of pulses per location to 100-2,000.
Modify operating parameters if sufficient clot lysis is not achieved or bubble activity extends beyond the model vessel.
Use the manufacturer's protocol or programming platform to set source parameters (Step 4.3).
Run the histotripsy source in degassed water without obstruction.
Increase applied voltage until a bubble cloud forms.
Adjust imaging array position using real-time imaging until the bubble cloud is centered on the image window.
Tighten screws to secure the imaging array firmly in the transducer opening.
Remove the clot from the pipette by cutting the sealed end with pliers.
Let the clot slide into a Petri dish along with the serum.
Cut the clot to 1 cm length using a scalpel, aiming for a uniform piece from the center of the clot.
Use a cleaning wipe to blot the cut section of the clot gently to remove excess fluid.
Place the clot section gently on a weighing scale and record the weight.
Manually raise the flow channel out of the water tank.
Remove the model vessel from the flow channel.
Place the clot in the model vessel using tweezers.
Attach the model vessel again to the flow channel.
Lower the flow channel into the tank with the proximal end low relative to the distal side.
Add 30 mL of plasma to the reservoir using a pipette.
Monitor the temperature until it reaches at least 36 °C.
Dispense rt-PA (80.4 µg in 30 mL of plasma, 2.68 µg/mL) into the plasma reservoir with a pipette.
Stir the plasma with the pipette to ensure uniform rt-PA distribution within the reservoir.
Draw plasma into the flow channel from the reservoir via the syringe pump until it fills the model vessel.
Use short pump draws at 60 mL/min if necessary to force plasma downstream the clot.
Manually draw through the syringe if needed to move the clot past the nylon rod.
Refill the reservoir with additional plasma/rt-PA to maintain 30 mL of solution in the flow channel.
Align the imaging array parallel to the length of the clot using the motorized positioners.
Level the model vessel manually and visually ensure no air bubbles are present using the imaging window.
Align the imaging array such that the imaging plane is perpendicular to the orientation described in step 6.2 using the motorized positioners.
Move the histotripsy source to the proximal end of the clot relative to the reservoir using motorized positioners.
Adjust the histotripsy source position so that the marked focal point aligns with the center of the clot.
Determine the insonation path along the length of the clot.
Set three waypoints along the length of the clot in 5 mm increments.
Align the first waypoint at the most proximal end of the clot relative to the reservoir.
Place the third waypoint in the distal position relative to the reservoir.
Fire test pulses from the histotripsy source with reduced exposure to 10 total pulses before finalizing each waypoint.
Adjust the position of the histotripsy source using motorized positioners if necessary to contain bubble activity within the clot.
Save the motor positions at each waypoint using commands provided by the manufacturer.
Run the syringe pump at 0.65 mL/min.
Wait for meniscus of the plasma to move.
Interpolate the path created in step 7.1.3 with intermediate steps between established waypoints.
Use a fixed step size smaller than half the width of the focal region.
Move the histotripsy source using motorized positioners at each path location.
Apply insonation parameters defined in step 4.8.
Monitor/image bubble activity during application of the histotripsy pulse at each path location.
Center the image on the histotripsy focus with dimensions covering 15 mm in azimuth and range.
Acquire a B-mode image prior to applying the histotripsy pulse.
Create a script in a programming platform to establish communication with the scanner.
Implement the acquisition of acoustic emissions in the script in step 7.2.3 to form passive cavitation images post hoc.
Acquire one passive cavitation image after every 10 treatment pulses.
Apply a flat time gain compensation of 50 at 8 incremental depths until the end of the imaging depth.
Adjust the transducer position in situ with motorized positioners if off-target bubble clouds are present.
Monitor for missed triggers of the imaging array and adjust the number of acquired imaging data sets accordingly.
Manually raise the model vessel out of the water tank to drain the perfusate via gravity.
Keep the flow channel levelled during draining to prevent clot movement downstream.
Collect the entire perfusate for further analysis in a small beaker by drawing plasma solution from the flow channel through the syringe pump at a very low flow rate.
Disconnect the model vessel and remove the clot, injecting a small amount of saline if necessary to dislodge the clot.
Wipe the clot similar to step 1.2.3.
Weigh the clot on the weighing scale for assessing the clot mass loss.
Add 100 mg of aminocaproic acid to a microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL of perfusate to the tube containing aminocaproic acid and mix well using a pipette.
Perform a latex immune-turbidimetric assay to quantify D-dimer in the sample.
Add 1 mL of perfusate to centrifuge tubes.
Spin at 610 x g (3,500 rpm) for 10 min.
Combine 0.5 mL of supernatant with 0.5 mL of Drabkins solution.
Let the mixture rest at room temperature for 15 min.
Transfer 200 µL to well plates.
Use a plate reader to read absorbance at 540 nm.
Cut a section from the center of the clot, approximately 2-3 mm in length with a scalpel.
Add the section to a cassette, maintaining its orientation relative to the direction of histotripsy pulse propagation.
Add 2 mL of low gelling agarose solution into the cassette to fix the clot in place.
Fix the sample in 10% formalin for 24 h.
Place the sample in 70% alcohol after 24 h.
Perform standard hemotoxylin-eosin staining.
Process signals from the imaging array using a robust Capon beamformer algorithm.
Create an image of acoustic emissions generated by the bubble cloud at each treatment location.
Segment the B-mode image to distinguish between clot and model vessel pixels.
Co-register the passive cavitation image with the B-mode image.
Sum up the acoustic energy within the clot over the exposure period.
